newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS SETTLE FOR ONE-YEAR DEAL WITH FREROTTE.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-REDSKINS SETTLE FOR ONE-YEAR DEAL WITH FREROTTE.

text.p: The Washington Redskins were unable to sign quarterback Gus Frerotte to a multi-year deal, but settled with him on a one-year contract before the start of training camp, the team said Monday.
Terms were not disclosed, but it is believed that Frerotte received a deal worth more than $1 million.

Frerotte, a seventh-round pick from Tulsa in 1994, won the starting job from Heath Shuler in last year's training camp and led the Redskins to a 7-1 record in the first half of the season. But Washington struggled to a 2-6 mark in the second half and barely missed the playoffs with a 9-7 record.
Frerotte passed for 3,453 yards last season, second only to Brett Favre in the NFC. He completed 57 percent of his passes with 12 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.

The Redskins signed veteran Jeff Hostetler on June 18th, one day after he was waived by the Oakland Raiders, to serve as a backup to Frerotte. Hostetler completed 60 percent of his passes for 2,548 yards with 23 touchdowns and 14 interceptions in 13 games last season. The Redskins had been searching for a backup to Frerotte since dealing Shuler to New Orleans in April.
The Redskins begin training camp on Thursday at Frostburg State.
